episode.title: The Real Reason France Used Guillotines In 1977!

synopsis: France conducted its final guillotine execution in 1977, an astonishing historical overlap with the premiere of Star Wars.
narration: France's final execution by guillotine occurred in 1977, an astonishing fact. This medieval method of capital punishment was still in use the very same year that Star Wars premiered, showcasing a stark contrast in human progress.

shots.prompt: A dramatic, low-angle shot of the base of a guillotine, weathered wood and dull metal blades. A single drop of water slowly falls, catching the harsh, clinical light, hinting at its grim function. The composition is stark and cold, emphasizing its outdated brutality.

A vibrant, colorful, and slightly chaotic close-up of a 1977 movie theater marquee, buzzing with neon lights, prominently displaying "STAR WARS" in classic typography. Excited crowds in period fashion mill about in the foreground, their faces alight with anticipation, a stark contrast to the previous shot.

music: A dramatically contrasting score. It opens with a dark, ominous, and percussive rhythm reminiscent of historical drama, then subtly shifts to incorporate futuristic, slightly unsettling synth elements, maintaining a driving, almost jarring pace. The music reflects both an antiquated past and an emerging future, creating a sense of temporal dissonance, concluding with an abrupt, unresolved synth chord.
